description: Agent Logistics: submit one carrier’s billed charges and applied terms with what was agreed for the shipment: the agreement with its currency, the base rate, each surcharge with its amount, the liability limit, the declared value, the pickup day and place, the days to file a claim and its text; the carrier’s record with its currency, the base rate billed, each surcharge billed with its amount, the total billed, the liability limit and declared value in its terms as applied, its claims window and its text; and optionally the pickup record with the day the carrier picked up and where. The signed report gives the agreement, the carrier’s record, the base rate billed against the agreed rate with the difference, every billed surcharge matched to an agreed one with its status as agreed, over, under, unagreed or not billed, the billed total against the rate and surcharges, the liability limit and declared value on each side, the pickup day and place against the agreement with the days late, and the claims window on each side, and counts them, and names a breach of terms: a base rate billed over the agreed rate, a surcharge the agreement does not hold, a surcharge billed over its agreed amount, a liability limit or declared value below the agreed figure, and a claims window shorter than agreed; then a total that does not equal its rate and surcharges, a declared value raised above the agreed one, a late pickup, a pickup at another place and a bill in another currency, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No base rate on both sides, or a liability limit, declared value, claims window or pickup day agreed with none on the carrier’s record leaves the carrier’s terms unverified. This reads one carrier’s billed charges and applied terms against the agreement for a shipment: a fee schedule against a quote or invoice is wever_fee-evidence-check, a quote against the charge settled for a paid call is wever_price-truth-check and provider quotes compared side by side are wever_quote-compare. Verdict logistics_carrier_breach, logistics_carrier_partial, logistics_carrier_unverified or logistics_carrier_per_terms. POST /api/logistics-carrier-check. Reads the logistics records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment, shipment booking, label purchase or external write. Agent Logistics reads a shipment’s logistics records after the fact, from the shipment’s own records: the shipment record against the order it serves, the promised delivery window against the booking and the arrival, the carrier’s terms against what was agreed, the tracking events for one shipment, the address across the order, the label and the carrier record, the customs material for a cross-border shipment, proof of delivery against the delivery terms and exception handling when something went wrong. Beside it, wever_shipping-check reads a shipping promise against its delivery evidence and reports the dispatch, delivery and cost mismatches with the days late and the amount over, while a logistics check reads one shipment’s booking, carrier, tracking, address, customs, delivery and exception records against the order, the promise made to the buyer and the terms agreed; wever_vendor-delivery-check reads a vendor’s whole delivery promise before the spend, while a logistics check reads one shipment’s own records after it shipped; and wever_boutique-record-shipment and wever_boutique-confirm-delivery record and confirm a boutique order’s shipment and delivery, while a logistics check reads the records and changes none. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-logistics-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-logistics/.
